clue.text: Get rid of money that's source of rancour

parts.note: cash is ready money
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so take the opening letter of rancour

explanation.surface: Someone is told to throw away money because it only breeds bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: IE stands for 'that is', which the clue gives as 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier an officer is to dismiss him from service, discharging him in disgrace.

clue.text: Where birds fight for room to manoeuvre

definitions.meaning: a pit where gamecocks were set to fight
the compartment from which a pilot manoeuvres an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A cockfighting arena is a cockpit, and so is the flight deck where a pilot sits.

clue.text: Match brought forward

definitions.meaning: something that strikes, as a match is struck

explanation.definitionFit: Anything that strikes can be called this, and in football it names an attacking forward.

clue.text: Do nothing right-typical of him!

parts.note: to idle is to do nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that a lazy person can never get anything right.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazybones is exactly the sort of person who does nothing, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Colour at reprimand confers honour

parts.note: red is a colour
to carpet someone is to call them in for a telling-off

explanation.surface: Being told off in a flush of embarrassment somehow ends with an award.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'carpet' is British slang for summoning someone for a reprimand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out a crimson rug for a guest is a mark of special respect.

clue.text: Look into abandoned chest for dresses

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other, so the short word sits within the jumbled letters
abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of chest are rearranged

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone peers into a chest left behind, hoping to find frocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dresses' looks like a plural noun, but it is the verb: clothes as in clothes a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs: to dress someone is to put garments on them.

clue.text: Rebuke hid in church

indicators.note: in places the word hid inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded for hiding in church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide is to scold or reprove.

clue.text: Feeling bad, not on the green for instance

parts.note: off means not on, as a switch
green is an example of a colour

explanation.surface: A golfer feels unwell when not on the putting green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the green' suggests golf, but it is just an example of a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-colour is a British idiom for slightly unwell.

clue.text: Difficult to start pushing this type of car

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so take the opening of pushing

explanation.surface: A car that is hard to get going and needs a push.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid roof, a particular body style.

clue.text: One looks everywhere for a rubber

definitions.meaning: a pad that rubs pans clean

explanation.definitionFit: A searcher who combs an area and an abrasive pad for pans share this name.

clue.text: Went round and round to Delius' first

parts.note: a round is a ring, a circle

indicators.note: first here asks for the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: Someone keeps circling back to the music of the composer Delius.
explanation.definitionFit: To circle is to travel round something, so the past tense means travelled around.

clue.text: Deduce nobody lacks substance in hell

parts.note: to infer is to deduce or conclude

indicators.note: lacks means the word is missing the piece that follows, so it is dropped out of nobody

parts.note: body means substance, as in a wine with body

explanation.surface: A thinker concludes that nobody in the underworld has any real substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacks' takes BODY out of NOBODY, leaving NO.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging blaze, and Dante's Inferno is the name for the infernal regions.

clue.text: Game to resist it offers no expressions

parts.note: poker is a card game
to face something is to confront or resist it

explanation.surface: A card game in which you must hold out against showing any feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A blank, unreadable countenance gives away no emotion, as card players cultivate.

clue.text: Cad executed animal

indicators.note: an executed person may be beheaded, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a rotter is a cad, a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A scoundrel was put to death, along with some creature.
explanation.walkthrough: Execution here means beheading: ROTTER loses its head, R.
explanation.definitionFit: This river-dwelling mammal with webbed feet is one kind of animal.

clue.text: Goes from container in case of threats

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other here
the case of a word is its outside, so take the first and last letters of threats

parts.note: an urn is a container, for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a box when danger threatens.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun: one's goes in a game are one's chances to play, as in taking turns.

clue.text: If sitting, have a drink first

indicators.note: first puts the drinking piece before the sitting piece

parts.note: to sup is to drink
sitting for a portrait is posing

explanation.surface: An artist's model should have a drink before sitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both introduce a condition: supposing that it rains means if it rains.

clue.text: A pure pose when displayed is very foggy

indicators.note: a display is laid out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A model's innocent posture, once shown, turns out to be murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displayed' rearranges A PURE POSE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea-souper is a thick yellowish fog, once typical of London; the clue uses it as an adjective for very foggy weather.

clue.text: Off to a dance with student, for a story

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver's plate, a student

explanation.surface: Someone heads to a dance with a student, ready to tell a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges TO A DANCE into ANECDOTA; the L-plate shows a learner, hence student.
explanation.definitionFit: Anecdotal describes evidence that comes from a tale rather than study.

clue.text: Sea dog, for example, about to get explosive

parts.note: salt suggests the sea, as in the salt water of the ocean
a dog is an example of a pet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: An old sailor and his dog are about to blow up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea dog' looks like one unit meaning an old sailor (SALT), but the setter splits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the key ingredient in gunpowder.

clue.text: The way pictures allow no time for surprise

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
art means pictures and paintings

indicators.note: no here means without, so the letter that follows is dropped from let

parts.note: to let is to allow

explanation.surface: A gallery leaves no time to be surprised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no time' takes T out of LET, leaving LE.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give someone a sudden shock or surprise.

clue.text: A lot of noise in support when ahead

indicators.note: in places the noise inside the support

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
a din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: Fans make a racket in support when their side is winning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' looks like 'plenty of', but A is a piece and DIN is the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A team leading is in front, ahead of its rivals.

clue.text: About to raise VAT, offer a counter argument

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: raising a word lifts it end over end, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a vat is a large tub

explanation.surface: A minister is about to put up value added tax, and someone objects.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the British sales tax, but here it is a tub; 'raise' turns TUB into BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to refute or argue against a claim.

clue.text: Troops ordered to take equipment inside

indicators.note: inside puts the equipment within the ordered word

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, ordered
a rig is a set of equipment

explanation.surface: Soldiers are told to take their kit indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a large military formation of soldiers.

clue.text: Beat chap to the Circle Line

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone beats up a man and heads for a London Underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground line, but here it is a line touching a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent is a straight line touching a curve at one point.

clue.text: A pound a minute for hard fought battle

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from libra
a mo is a moment, a minute

explanation.surface: Paying a pound a minute for a fierce contest.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British slang for a moment, as in 'wait a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: The siege of the Alamo in Texas in 1836 was a famous last stand.

clue.text: eg Press get into dubious act of appeasement

parts.note: the press is an example of the media

indicators.note: something dubious is unsound or shady, so the letters of into are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reporters get mixed up in a questionable attempt at peace-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dubious' looks attached to 'act', but it rearranges INTO to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediation is intervention to settle a dispute and pacify the parties.

clue.text: Rumoured to look after set charges

indicators.note: a rumour is something spoken of, so a word that sounds alike is wanted

parts.note: to mind is to look after

explanation.surface: Gossip has it that someone will look after the fees.
explanation.definitionFit: Mined means laid with explosives, set with explosive charges.

clue.text: A fork mostly providing protection in the kitchen

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a prong is a tine of a fork

explanation.surface: A fork is handy for safety in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is a garment worn over clothes to protect them while cooking.

clue.text: Teaching lacking in instinct

indicators.note: lacking means going without the small word that follows, so it is removed

parts.note: intuition is instinct, a gut feeling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lessons that go without any natural instinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in' looks like a phrase, but 'in' is the piece removed from INTUITION.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is instruction given by a tutor.

clue.text: Where football chants can lead to row

definitions.meaning: the standing banks at a football ground, where supporters start the singing
a row of joined houses along a street

explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is both a stepped bank of standing room at a stadium and a row of houses built as one block.

clue.text: Ringed? Rung. Rang? No

definitions.meaning: having been given an engagement ring, so promised in marriage
a phone call made but not answered because the line is busy

explanation.definitionFit: Betrothed people wear a ring, and a busy telephone line gives the caller no connection.

clue.text: Allowed to take nine letters and 8 got indulgent

annotationWithheld.why: 'Allowed to take nine letters and 8 got indulgent': LET (allowed) around ENIEN would give LENIENT, but '8 got' does not supply E as held and no source or scan confirms the printed wording; 8-down is SCOURER.
annotationWithheld.clue: Allowed to take nine letters and 8 got indulgent
